messages:
Priya: quick sync after the postmortem review. we need to finalize owners for SLO/SLA edits, a migration playbook for tiered SLOs, and a dashboard to track recurrence windows. short and actionable pls.

Jamal: agree. can you list the concrete actions you want tracked?

Priya: yes. draft here: (A) Tiered SLO migration doc + customer-facing note (owner: Jamal; due: 2024-12-01). (B) Dashboard: recurrence-window panel (show successive p95 exceedances over 7d), per-tenant tail heatmap, and deploy-annotator; owner: Lucia; due: 2024-11-29. (C) Runbook/playbook: step-by-step for moving traffic between Dedicated/Hosted during bursts + rollback checklist; owner: Nikhil; due: 2024-11-24. (D) Error-budget automation: auto-create incident card when burn > 15% sustained 20m; owner: Morgan; due: 2024-11-25. (E) Synthetic suite: warm-path canary + linear ramp test to detect cold-start regressions; owner: Lucia; due: 2024-11-23.

Lucia: for the dashboard i'll add a recurrence-window viz that marks contiguous SLO-violating windows and a small table listing deploy IDs overlapping each window. link wip: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/slo/migration-2149990

Nikhil: playbook ack. i'll include traffic-shifting commands and a staging checklist. sample commands: ```bash
# shift 10% traffic to dedicated pool
rdw-traffic-shift --from hosted --to dedicated --percent 10 --note "emergency shift"
# rollback
rdw-traffic-shift --rollback-last
```
I'll also add a 'when to escalate' decision tree.

Morgan: automation note: team agreed to not change error budget calc, but to add auto-ticketing when burn crosses thresholds. i'll wire alerts to create a postmortem card if sustained > 1hr. will also add pager tags.

Jamal: for the SLO doc: i propose we define three tiers (standard/premium/dedicated) with explicit p95 targets and a migration window. draft wording for customers: "Standard tier transitional p95 <= 220ms for 30 days while we stabilize; Premium p95 <= 180ms; Dedicated negotiated." i'll submit PR and include audit trail referencing incident 2024-11-19. PR ETA 2024-11-30.

Priya: good. who will own the customer notification if we change SLOs? need legal review too.

Jamal: i'll own customer notice + tag legal for review in the PR.

oncall-bot: Incident #2024-11-19-17 closed. Postmortem uploaded to docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/pm/2024-11-19-cache-tail-postmortem

Lucia: synthetic plan: canary warm hits every 5m + linear ramp (50 -> 500 qps) hourly for 10m to catch throughput regressions. script snippet: ```bash
rdw-synth --job warm-canary --freq 5m --keys 20
rdw-synth --job ramp-test --pattern linear --from 50 --to 500 --duration 10m
```
I'll add panels for canary hit-rate and failure count.

Morgan: about paging behavior for auto-ticket: propose critical -> immediate page SRE primary + create incident card; high -> slack notify + create ticket but no page. i'll implement.

Priya: timeline recap: SLO doc (Jamal) 11/30, migration playbook (Nikhil) 11/24, dashboard + canary (Lucia) 11/29 & 11/23, error-budget automation (Morgan) 11/25. i'll create the follow-up tracker and schedule a weekly 15m check-in until all closed.

Lucia: small ask  do we want the dashboard to surface top 5 tenants by recurrence count? could help product triage.

Priya: yes please. add tenant-anonymized identifiers by default, and make raw tenant IDs available to SRE + product via a button.

Jamal: adding note to PR to include an entry in the SLA change log. also will add a FAQ blurb for customers about temporary p95 shifts.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: dashboards/slo-migration-panels by Lucia -> staging. ETA 2024-11-26 04:00 UTC.

Priya: thanks all. owners update the tracker when you start; i'll ping daily for the next week. :white_check_mark:
